title: Jujutsu Kaisen: Shimetsu Kaiyuu - Zenpen
content:
You’d never hear me talk about Jujutsu Kaisen in any circle except that I’d be calling it mid left and right and throughout. People get very offended with the word for some reason. Mid does not mean bad, it’s just mid, average, mediocre. The Hidden Inventory and Premature Dead arc’s adaptation in season two was the first disturbance in my bias against the series, but I still stood my ground. “Sure, this are is the outlier in this series” I arrogantly asserted, but the Culling Game arc’s adaptation in this season had me reconsider my aggression.

While watching this season specifically, I started to feel forthe first time that I really enjoy watching the series. Am I being held hostage as some kind of Stockholm Syndrome? Maybe, but I loved every second of it.

You’d hear people glaze the animation very specifically, when talking about the show, but more than ever, this season has proven to be the series at its peak when it comes to production all round. It feels like everything got upgraded in terms of consistency. I can go all on and praise every aspect about art direction, storyboarding, cinematography, framing, pacing, sound, voice acting, direction… and so on, bit it’s the consistency that sells for me. Never have I felt like an episode dropped the quality ever so slightly than the one before. A perfectly coherent entertainment sandwich, which the perfectly consistent amount of sauce spread all over it.

A very popular criticism concerning this season is the absurd excessive exposition. I don’t blame most of the fandom. The majority of fans are unfortunately TikTok clip watchers, that’s how they keep up with the show, that, and constantly frying their mind, high on agenda brainrot. It is only normal that they would have negative reading tolerance, let alone comprehenssion.

Yes, there was a lot of exposition dumps and yes, the directions absolutely nailed the delivery. It felt like reading one of those colorful kids magazines full of cool illustrations from childhood. For the first time in the show I thought the dialog was no longer weak. Thanks not only to the great wiring and voice acting, but also storyboarding. Yeah, storyboarding for dialog that played better than some series’ big fights.

At this point, I feel like the only big issue with this season was that it’s not long enough. Part two can’t come soon enough.

Overall: 9.18/10.
